report.executive_summary: A critical incident was reconstructed from source IP 203.0.113.45 on server-01. Detected stages: ssh brute force, login after brute force, privilege escalation, sensitive data access, exfiltration.
report.attack_narrative: 27 failed SSH logins from 203.0.113.45 → Successful SSH login as admin → sudo/root shell detected → Sensitive file access: /etc/shadow, /var/backups/db.sql → Outbound transfer of 1.80 GB to 203.0.113.45
why_detected: Deterministic detection rules verified each stage against explicit operational thresholds.
SSH_BRUTE_FORCE: 27 failed SSH logins from 203.0.113.45 (seed: same source_ip + host)
LOGIN_AFTER_BRUTE_FORCE: Successful SSH login as admin (seed: same source_ip + host within 10 min of brute-force alert)
PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION: sudo/root shell detected (session pivot: same user + host after suspicious login)
SENSITIVE_DATA_ACCESS: Sensitive file access: /etc/shadow, /var/backups/db.sql (session pivot: same user + host after suspicious login)
EXFILTRATION: Outbound transfer of 1.80 GB to 203.0.113.45 (session stage chain: same host within 15 min of prior stage)
Incident reached deterministic severity score of 100/100 (critical).

Controlled MITRE ATT&CK mapping: T1110.001 (Brute Force: Password Guessing), T1078 (Valid Accounts), T1548.003 (Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Sudo and Sudo Caching), T1005 (Data from Local System), T1048 (Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol).
report.potential_impact: The observed activity is consistent with unauthorized outbound data transfer and potential data leakage, unauthorized access to sensitive system or credential files, administrative privilege escalation via sudo, unauthorized access via compromised credentials following brute force. Validate scope and affected credentials before taking containment action.
investigation_steps: Verify the SSH source IP and affected account in authoritative authentication logs.
Review privileged commands executed during the suspicious session.
Validate accessed file paths and outbound transfer destinations against known business activity.
Preserve relevant event logs and volatile memory before making containment changes.
